semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL3 contract states the EmergencyStopping state 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal,' attributing emission to the state. In the FCSTM, event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8 is consumed as a trigger at the inner level (transitions 22-24) causing entry into the state, not as an effect emitted by it. The state's only outgoing transition (line 34) is triggered by exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected (line 9), a different event, with no effect field. No transition from or within EmergencyStopping carries 'Obstacle Detected' as a sent signal. The exact binding resolves all five element references. The strongest alternative reading is that the PlantUML source label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' on line 19 can be interpreted as an effect (the state sends this upon exit), which would behaviorally satisfy the NL. The source notation is genuinely ambiguous between trigger and effect readings, and the FCSTM chose the trigger formalization. This undercutting reading survives because the source text supports it, even though the FCSTM's formal representation contradicts it.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The PlantUML source transition label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' (line 19) can be read as the state sending the signal upon exit, which would satisfy the NL's effect obligation; the FCSTM's formalization of this label as an input trigger (event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected) is one interpretation among compatible readings of the source notation.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL9 contract states 'In the Approaching substate, the system sends the Send signal,' requiring the state to actively emit the signal as an output effect. The FCSTM transition:line:18 (Approaching to [*]) has triggers=[exit_Send] and effects=[R45RouteToken=7]. No state-level or transition-level effect on Approaching emits a 'Send' signal. The event exit_Send (line 6) appears only as an input trigger, meaning it must be supplied externally rather than produced by the state. The exact binding resolves all three element references. The strongest alternative reading is that the PlantUML source label 'exit/Send' on line 14 is ambiguous: in UML statechart notation, a transition label can represent either a trigger or an effect. Reading it as an effect (the state sends this upon exit) would satisfy the NL's obligation. The FCSTM chose the trigger formalization. This undercutting reading survives because the source text genuinely supports both interpretations.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The PlantUML source transition label 'exit/Send' (line 14) can be read as the state emitting the signal upon exit, which would satisfy the NL's effect obligation; the FCSTM's representation of this label as an input trigger (event:exit_Send) is a compatible formalization choice that preserves the behavioral meaning of the source.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The Approaching state must emit the 'Send' signal as an output effect while active in the substate per the NL9 contract.

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL9 requirement quote, PlantUML line 14 (transition label 'exit/Send'), FCSTM event:exit_Send:line:6 (opaque trigger), FCSTM transition:line:18 (triggers=[exit_Send], effects=[R45RouteToken=7]), FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 (no exit action).
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL9 clause states 'the system sends the Send signal' while in the Approaching substate. The PlantUML source (line 14) uses 'Approaching --> InMotion:exit/Send' as a transition label. In UML, 'exit/Action' on a state means performing the action on exit, but placed on a transition label it becomes an opaque event name in the closed model (event:exit_Send:line:6). The FCSTM transition:line:18 has this as its trigger, not as an effect. The transition's only effect is R45RouteToken=7. The 'Send' action is never executed; the transition waits for an externally supplied event literally named 'exit/Send'. The strongest rebuttal is that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' and the divergence is between author text and declaration semantics. However, this is a W-level observation about the source-to-model mapping, not a semantic alternative reading of the NL obligation. The NL requires the state to send the signal, and the model provides no mechanism for the state to do so. No competent semantic defeater survives.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The 'Send' signal must be a state action (exit effect) of the Approaching state as the NL requires, but the source uses lifecycle syntax 'exit/Send' as a transition label, which the closed model represents as an opaque event trigger rather than an executable effect.

Where the NL uses more descriptive language (e.g., 'includes the actions', 'sends the signal', 'continues to approach'), a secondary loose-reading is compatible with the facts, yielding undercutting survivors. The V1 dead-end case (Stopping) is established with no terminal support. The initial-entry case (i13) is genuinely unresolved due to non-precise binding. Source-to-model lowering artifacts (opaque transition labels) are treated as W-boundary issues, not D-level semantic alternatives.

decisions.basis: Dossier for obligation 0024:r2:i5: NL3 requirement quote, FCSTM transition:line:34 facts (triggers=[exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected], effects=[]), event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected:line:9 (input trigger only), PlantUML source line 19, and exact element binding.
decisions.reason: The NL3 contract states the EmergencyStopping state 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal,' requiring the state to actively emit the signal as an effect. The FCSTM transition:line:34 (EmergencyStopping to InMotion) has triggers=[exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected] and effects=[]. The event exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected (line 9) appears only as an input trigger, meaning it must be supplied externally rather than produced by the state. The exact binding resolves all three element references. The strongest alternative reading is that the PlantUML source label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' on line 19 is ambiguous: in UML statechart notation, a transition label can represent either a trigger or an effect. Reading it as an effect (the state sends this upon exit) would satisfy the NL's obligation. The FCSTM chose the trigger formalization. issues.basis: NL3 segment; contract NL-CONTRACT-NL3-ACTION-1 (state=EmergencyStopping, action=Emergency Stop, no phase); FCSTM state EmergencyStopping named 'EmergencyStopping\n[PlantUML body] Emergency Stop' (description only, no action field); reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory=[]; source PlantUML line 'EmergencyStopping: Emergency Stop' (state description, not entry/do/exit action).
issues.expected: The EmergencyStopping state has a formal action 'Emergency Stop' as required by the NL.
issues.observed: The FCSTM state EmergencyStopping has no formal action field; 'Emergency Stop' appears only in the state's display name string. The reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory is empty (count=0), confirming no actions are formally present in the model.
issues.reason: The NL requires a state_action property on EmergencyStopping with value 'Emergency Stop'. The binding hints specify state and action but no lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit), so S4 is not applicable. The FCSTM has no formal action on this state, and the inspection facts confirm zero actions model-wide. This is a precise semantic gap: the NL describes an action that the model does not formally represent.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source uses 'EmergencyStopping: Emergency Stop' as a state description label, and one could argue the NL's 'includes the actions' language is loosely describing the state's purpose rather than a formal UML action. However, the NL explicitly uses the word 'actions' and the model has no action representation.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping state lacks formal action 'Emergency Stop'

issues.basis: NL3 segment; contract NL-CONTRACT-NL3-EFFECT-1 (state=EmergencyStopping, effect=Obstacle Detected); FCSTM event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8 consumed by transitions 22/23/24 (inner exits); FCSTM transition:line:34 trigger=exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected (different event); source tr_0009 event='Obstacle Detected' (entry trigger); source tr_0010 event='exit/Send Obstacle Detected' (exit, different name).
issues.expected: The EmergencyStopping state produces or sends the 'Obstacle Detected' signal as an effect of its operation.
issues.observed: In the FCSTM, 'Obstacle Detected' (event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8) is the trigger for inner exit transitions (lines 22-24) that cause entry into EmergencyStopping via the route-token mechanism. It is not an effect emitted by the EmergencyStopping state. The state's only outgoing transition (line:34) is triggered by 'exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected', a different event. No effect field on any transition from or within EmergencyStopping contains 'Obstacle Detected' as a sent signal.
issues.reason: The NL requires an effect of sending 'Obstacle Detected' on the EmergencyStopping state. The FCSTM represents 'Obstacle Detected' as the entry trigger (consumed at inner level), not as an effect of the state. The state's exit uses a different event name. This is a direction mismatch: the NL says the state emits the signal, the model says the signal causes entry to the state.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the NL's 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal' is a loose description of the state's purpose (it exists because an obstacle was detected) rather than a formal emission requirement. The exit event 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' partially contains the text. However, the NL grammatically attributes the sending to the state itself ('which...sends'), and the exact signal name 'Obstacle Detected' differs from 'Send Obstacle Detected'.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping does not send 'Obstacle Detected' as an effect; it is the entry trigger

issues.basis: NL8 segment; contract NL-CONTRACT-NL8-ACTION-1 (state=Accelerating, phase=entry, action=Accelerate); FCSTM state:Accelerating:line:11 (no action field); PlantUML source line 6 'Accelerating: Accelerating' (description only); reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory=[]; verify_facts initial-entry:transition:line:14 proved (entry edge exists but carries no action).
issues.expected: The Accelerating state has an entry action 'Accelerate' as specified by the NL's 'Entry/Accelerate' notation.
issues.observed: The FCSTM state Accelerating (line:11) has no formal action field; its name string is 'Accelerating\n[PlantUML body] Accelerating' which is just the state description repeated. The PlantUML source shows 'Accelerating: Accelerating' (description only, no 'entry Accelerate' construct). The reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory is empty.
issues.reason: The NL requires a state_action with phase=entry and action=Accelerate on the Accelerating state. The binding hints provide all three S4 inputs (state=Accelerating, phase=entry, action=Accelerate). The FCSTM has no entry action on this state. The PlantUML source also lacks an 'entry' construct. This is a clear S4 violation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The state description 'Accelerating' is semantically close to the action 'Accelerate', and one could argue the description implies the entry behavior. However, UML state diagrams distinguish between state descriptions and formal entry/do/exit actions, and the NL explicitly uses the 'Entry/Accelerate' notation which maps to a formal entry action.
issues.title: Accelerating state lacks entry action 'Accelerate'

issues.basis: NL9 segment; contract NL-CONTRACT-NL9-ACTION-1 (state=Approaching, action='approach the destination', no phase hint); FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 (no action field); PlantUML source 'Approaching: Approaching' (description only); reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory=[].
issues.expected: The Approaching state has a formal ongoing (do) activity representing 'approach the destination'.
issues.observed: The FCSTM state Approaching (line:13) has no formal action field; its name string is 'Approaching\n[PlantUML body] Approaching'. The PlantUML source shows 'Approaching: Approaching' (description only, no 'do' construct). The reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory is empty.
issues.reason: The NL requires a state_action (ongoing activity) on Approaching with value 'approach the destination'. No lifecycle phase is specified in the binding hints (the NL says 'continues to' which implies do, but the contract extraction did not assign a phase). Without an explicit phase, S4 is not applicable. The model has no formal action on this state. This is a precise predicate-null gap.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The state name 'Approaching' itself semantically implies the ongoing activity of approaching, and the NL's 'continues to approach the destination' could be read as describing the state's purpose rather than requiring a formal do-action. However, the NL uses explicit action language ('continues to approach') that maps to a UML do-activity.
issues.title: Approaching state lacks ongoing activity 'approach the destination'

issues.basis: NL2 segment; transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 ALT-NL2-1 (event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived'); source tr_0008 (InMotion→Stopping, event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived'); FCSTM transition:line:30 (triggers=[], guard=R45RouteToken==8); FCSTM transitions 19/20/21 (inner exits with trigger=Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, effect=R45RouteToken=8); working_contract macro:transition:tr_0008 (segments 1-4).
issues.expected: The FCSTM transition from InMotion to Stopping is triggered by the event 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' as the NL specifies.
issues.observed: FCSTM transition:line:30 (InMotion→Stopping) has triggers=[] (empty) and guard='R45RouteToken == 8'. The event Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived is consumed at the inner level by transitions line:19, line:20, and line:21 (Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching → [*] with effect R45RouteToken=8), not on the outer InMotion→Stopping transition itself. The source transition tr_0008 explicitly has event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' on the InMotion→Stopping edge.
issues.reason: The transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 alternative ALT-NL2-1 specifies event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived' for the InMotion→Stopping relation. The source confirms this (tr_0008). The FCSTM outer transition (line:30) has an empty trigger list. This is a structural contrast between source and closed model at the exact transition locus: the event was decomposed to the inner level by the compiler, leaving the outer transition untriggered. The derived contract captures this trigger_set obligation that the NL-only extraction did not separately state as an atomic contract.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The compiler's route-token mechanism preserves the behavioral semantics: the event IS consumed in the model (at the inner level) and does ultimately cause the InMotion→Stopping transition. The trigger is relocated rather than lost. One could argue the NL's 'indicated by' language is satisfied by the causal chain even if the trigger is not on the exact transition. However, the contract property is trigger_set on the specific transition, and the FCSTM transition has no trigger.
issues.title: InMotion-to-Stopping transition lacks event trigger 'Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived'

issues.basis: NL10; FCSTM transitions:line:18 (exit_Send), :line:21 (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived), :line:24 (Obstacle_Detected) all source from state:Approaching:line:13; verify_facts confirm all are reachable
issues.expected: The system stays in Approaching and only exits when ready to stop or decelerate (planned stopping conditions)
issues.observed: FCSTM shows three exit transitions from Approaching: exit_Send (line 18), Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived (line 21), and Obstacle_Detected (line 24); the Obstacle_Detected exit represents an emergency condition that is semantically distinct from a planned 'ready to stop or decelerate' condition
issues.reason: The NL specifies retention until 'ready to stop or decelerate', which most naturally refers to planned stopping; the model permits exit via an emergency obstacle event that is a reactive condition rather than a readiness state, creating a possible retention violation
issues.requirement_quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Emergency stopping (Obstacle_Detected) results in stopping behavior and could be interpreted as a form of 'ready to stop' since the system does stop; under this broad reading, all three exits satisfy the retention condition
issues.title: Approaching can be exited via emergency Obstacle_Detected event not covered by 'ready to stop or decelerate'

semantic_adjudication.basis: Dossier for obligation 0024:r2:i1: NL3 requirement quote, FCSTM event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8 (inner-level trigger), event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected:line:9 (exit trigger, different name), transition:line:34 (no effect), PlantUML source line 19, and exact element binding.
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL3 contract states the EmergencyStopping state 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal,' attributing emission to the state. In the FCSTM, event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8 is consumed as a trigger at the inner level (transitions 22-24) causing entry into the state, not as an effect emitted by it. The state's only outgoing transition (line 34) is triggered by exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected (line 9), a different event, with no effect field. No transition from or within EmergencyStopping carries 'Obstacle Detected' as a sent signal. The exact binding resolves all five element references. The strongest alternative reading is that the PlantUML source label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' on line 19 can be interpreted as an effect (the state sends this upon exit), which would behaviorally satisfy the NL. The source notation is genuinely ambiguous between trigger and effect readings, and the FCSTM chose the trigger formalization. This undercutting reading survives because the source text supports it, even though the FCSTM's formal representation contradicts it.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The PlantUML source transition label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' (line 19) can be read as the state sending the signal upon exit, which would satisfy the NL's effect obligation; the FCSTM's formalization of this label as an input trigger (event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected) is one interpretation among compatible readings of the source notation.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The EmergencyStopping state must produce or send the 'Obstacle Detected' signal as an effect of its operation per the NL3 contract.

The exact binding resolves the state, transition, and event. The strongest alternative reading is that the state name 'Approaching' itself encodes the ongoing activity, and the NL's 'continues to approach' is a description of the state's purpose rather than a requirement for a separate formal action keyword. This undercutting reading survives because the state identity does semantically represent the behavior, even though no explicit action field exists.

The FCSTM transition:line:18 (Approaching to [*]) has triggers=[exit_Send] and effects=[R45RouteToken=7]. No state-level or transition-level effect on Approaching emits a 'Send' signal. semantic_adjudication.basis: NL9 requirement quote, PlantUML line 14 (transition label 'exit/Send'), FCSTM event:exit_Send:line:6 (opaque trigger), FCSTM transition:line:18 (triggers=[exit_Send], effects=[R45RouteToken=7]), FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 (no exit action).
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL9 clause states 'the system sends the Send signal' while in the Approaching substate. The PlantUML source (line 14) uses 'Approaching --> InMotion:exit/Send' as a transition label. In UML, 'exit/Action' on a state means performing the action on exit, but placed on a transition label it becomes an opaque event name in the closed model (event:exit_Send:line:6). The FCSTM transition:line:18 has this as its trigger, not as an effect. The transition's only effect is R45RouteToken=7. The 'Send' action is never executed; the transition waits for an externally supplied event literally named 'exit/Send'. The strongest rebuttal is that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' and the divergence is between author text and declaration semantics. However, this is a W-level observation about the source-to-model mapping, not a semantic alternative reading of the NL obligation. The NL requires the state to send the signal, and the model provides no mechanism for the state to do so. No competent semantic defeater survives.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The 'Send' signal must be a state action (exit effect) of the Approaching state as the NL requires, but the source uses lifecycle syntax 'exit/Send' as a transition label, which the closed model represents as an opaque event trigger rather than an executable effect.

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL3 requirement quote, PlantUML line 19 (transition label 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected'), FCSTM event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected:line:9 (opaque trigger), FCSTM transition:line:34 (trigger=exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected, no effect), FCSTM state:EmergencyStopping:line:28 (no exit action).
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL3 clause states the EmergencyStopping state 'sends the Obstacle Detected signal'. The PlantUML source (line 19) uses 'EmergencyStopping --> InMotion:exit/Send Obstacle Detected' as a transition label. In the closed model, this becomes an opaque event (event:exit_Send_Obstacle_Detected:line:9) that serves as the trigger for transition:line:34, not as an effect. The 'Send Obstacle Detected' action is never executed; the transition waits for an externally supplied event with that literal name. The strongest rebuttal is that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' and the divergence is between author text and declaration semantics. This is a W-level observation, not a semantic alternative reading of the NL obligation. The NL requires the state to send the signal, and the model provides no mechanism for the state to do so. No competent semantic defeater survives.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The 'Send Obstacle Detected' signal must be a state action (exit effect) of the EmergencyStopping state as the NL requires, but the source uses lifecycle syntax 'exit/Send Obstacle Detected' as a transition label, which the closed model represents as an opaque event trigger rather than an executable effect.
